title: Implantable contact lens (ICL)
what: The surgeon places a thin lens inside your eye, and your own lens stays in place. This corrects strong nearsightedness and other vision problems.
why: When you want vision correction, but laser is not right for you: high nearsightedness or a thin cornea.
duration: surgery usually takes 15 to 30 minutes per eye; you usually go home the same day
tell_doctor: All your medicines. The doctor will tell you if anything needs to change
If you had eye diseases or eye surgery
If you are pregnant or breastfeeding

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: A detailed eye exam is done before surgery. Contact lenses are stopped beforehand. The clinic will tell you how long.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: If you have sedation, the clinic will tell you when to stop eating.

prepare.title: Makeup
prepare.text: No makeup or face cream on the day of surgery.

steps: Drops are put in to widen the pupil and numb the eye
Sometimes you get a sedative through a vein
A small device holds your eyelids open
The surgeon makes a tiny cut
The folded lens is put in and opens up inside the eye
A protective shield is placed over your eye
feel: During surgery, you see light and feel pressure, not pain
Vision usually gets better within the first few days
after: Do not rub your eye or get it wet for a few days
No swimming pools or sports until your doctor allows
The second eye is usually done later
red_flags: Severe eye pain, nausea, or vomiting: see a doctor right away
A severe headache with eye pain: call emergency services

faq.a: Yes. If needed, the lens can be removed or replaced.

faq.q: Will I feel the lens in my eye?
faq.a: No, people usually do not feel it.

reminders.text: ICL surgery tomorrow. No makeup. Bring sunglasses and someone to go with you.
